member.title: TC Guide

sections.title: What The Title Commitment Agent Does
Deals, Closing Out And The Daily Email

member.html:
Who reads what. This is the guide for TCs. Read sections 1–11 and keep the Quick Reference Card handy. Team Leaders and Managers have their own guides with one more section (your photo → Help).
What's new in version 2. The Title Agent is now the Title Commitment Agent, at title.totalchb.com. It looks and works like the Universal Team Hub, you sign in with your company Google account, and its Closing Blockers show up in the hub as tasks (section 10). Old links from earlier emails still open the right deal. New in 2.1: the 8 AM email lists Closing Blockers only and goes out on time from Google Cloud; the Team Hub's date calendar; Team (Managers, from your photo) with roles and photos; Settings → Permissions for Team Leaders and Members; and picking who gets the email. New in 2.2: every export is also saved in the team's Google Drive folder, in a folder for its type, with the date and time in its name; and due dates take a time, as in the Team Hub. New in 2.3: Help under your photo, with the guide for your role. New in 2.4: Help works as in the Team Hub: the guide inside the app, the PDFs to open or download, and the Team Hub's delete passwords for Team Leaders and Managers. New in 2.5: the Team Hub's header, with its clock and Active (who's online).

01What The Title Commitment Agent Does

Upload a title commitment, and the Title Commitment Agent lists everything that has to happen before the deal can close, the way a senior title examiner would. Each item shows exactly where it came from, so you can check it in seconds.

What a review gives you

  • A list sorted by urgency: Closing Blockers first, then Before Closing, then Review / FYI.
  • For every item: what to do, who actually has to provide it, a due date counted back from closing, the amount when there is one, and the exact wording and page in the commitment.
  • Warnings when the commitment expires before your closing date, or when a numbered item could not be accounted for.
  • A live checklist the whole team sees: statuses, due dates and notes change on everyone's screen at once. Export it to PDF, Word, Excel, CSV or Google Sheets / Docs.
  • The Closing Blockers in the Universal Team Hub, kept in step both ways (section 10), and a summary email every weekday at 8:00 AM Eastern.
Important. The Title Commitment Agent does not replace the title company or the attorney, and it can be wrong. It makes sure nothing is overlooked. A person still checks the list and signs off before closing.

02Signing In

Only company Google accounts (@totalchb.com) can open it. There is no separate password.

  1. Go to title.totalchb.com and bookmark it.
  2. Click Sign In With Google and pick your @totalchb.com account.
  3. You stay signed in on that browser. Links from the daily email and from the Team Hub open straight to the deal.
  4. On a shared computer, click your initials at the top right, then Sign Out.
Tip. A personal Gmail or any other account is turned away with "doesn't have access. Use your @totalchb.com account." Sign in again with your company account.

03Finding Your Way Around

WhereWhat it's for
DEALSHome. Every reviewed deal, with search and Open / Closed / All. The numbers at the top count open deals, open Closing Blockers and deals closing in the next 7 days.
ANALYZEUpload a new or updated commitment (section 4).
TRAININGOptional: measure the agent on a commitment your team already worked (section 7).
KNOWLEDGEWhat the agent knows: the Feedback Inbox, the team's lessons and the professional checklist.
The clockEastern time from the website's own clock, in the colour of the connection: green when everything is saved, indigo while a change is on its way, red when it isn't saved or the page is offline. Click it for the details (and Retry Now when that's safe).
ActiveHow many of the team have the app open right now. Click it for who, and whether on a phone or a desktop (anyone seen in the last five minutes). On a phone: your photo → Who's Online.
Sun / moonLight or dark look. Your choice is remembered on that browser.
Your photoYour account and role, Settings, Team (Managers only), Help and Sign Out. Your initials show until a manager adds your photo.

Help

Your photo → Help (or Settings → Open Help) opens this guide inside the app, the one for your role, as the Team Hub's Help does: the TC Guide, the Team Leader Guide (with approving lessons and the Team Hub's delete passwords) or the Manager Guide. The contents are on the left (a row along the top on a tablet or phone) and the guide with its pictures on the right. At the top, Open or Download the PDF: a Team Leader's or Manager's own copy ends with a page of their delete passwords. Team Leaders can also send the TC Guide, and Managers all three, without passwords.

On a phone

Same link, same sign-in. The tabs move to a second row, every item is a card you tap to open, and menus slide up from the bottom. Everything works on a phone, uploads and exports included; a computer is easier for long lists.

04Reviewing A New Commitment

When the title company sends a commitment, run it through the agent before you do anything else.

  1. Click ANALYZE (or Analyze A Commitment on the Deals page).
  2. Drop the commitment PDF on Title Commitment (PDF), or click it to choose the file. Scanned PDFs are fine (PDF only, under 50 MB).
  3. Optional but recommended: add the Purchase Contract. The agent then checks the seller, buyer, price and dates against the commitment.
  4. Leave Is This An Updated Commitment… on No, a new deal (revised commitments: section 8).
  5. Click Read Documents. It takes about a minute; the step it's on shows as it goes.

Confirm the deal

The agent fills in the deal details from the documents. Check each one and fix anything that's off:

FieldWhat to check
Property Address / StateMatches the contract.
Deal TypeWholesale (Assignment), Double Close, Novation / Listing, Fix & Flip, Buy & Hold, Subject-To or Seller Financing. It changes which checks the agent runs, so get it right.
Closing DateClick it and pick the day on the calendar, then Set Closing Date. Every due date is counted back from it. If you don't know it yet, add it later and re-run.
TC (Owns Every Item)Who owns this deal's list: everyone in TC on Team.
Title CompanyUsually filled in from the commitment.
Notes For The AgentAnything it can't see in the documents, e.g. "seller is behind on payments".
  1. Look at the box at the top. Green Numbering check passed means every numbered requirement and exception was picked up. Red lists the item numbers to check by hand.
  2. Click Run Full Review. It takes 1–3 minutes: the agent writes the list, then a second, independent pass looks only for anything missing. You land on the deal when it's done.
Tip. You can keep working in another tab while it runs. If you refresh by mistake, the confirm screen comes back in the same tab. Start Over throws the upload away: nothing is saved as a deal until you click Run Full Review.

05Reading A Deal

The deal page is where you'll spend your time. Read it top to bottom the first time.

At the topMeaning
Deal type and Closing chipThe chip counts the days to closing; it turns orange inside 7 days and red once the date has passed.
Open BlockersClosing Blockers not yet Cleared or Waived. Red until there are none.
Items ClearedDone (Cleared or Waived) out of everything on the list. The bar below fills up as you go.
Coverage100% means every numbered item in Schedule B-I and B-II was accounted for. Anything less comes with a red Check by hand box naming the item numbers: read those yourself.
Watch out. If you see The commitment expires before closing, ask the title company for an updated commitment right away. Some commitments expire 30 days after their date, not 180.

The three priorities

PriorityWhat it meansTypical examples
Closing BlockerNeeds money paid to, or a document from, someone outside the closing table, or a court / government action. The deal can't close until it's done. These also go to the Team Hub.Mortgage payoffs and releases, lis pendens and pending foreclosures, judgments (even a prior owner's), tax lien certificates, taxes sold or certified as a lien, city and state tax liens, workers' comp liens, code and maintenance liens, delinquent utilities, wind/lease/option memoranda to terminate, errors in the commitment.
Before ClosingNeeded by closing day, but handled in the normal course.The deed, LLC documents, FinCEN details, HOA estoppel, affidavits, transfer forms, bring-down of an old commitment, taxes due or past due shown in Schedule B-II (paid at closing), a certified copy of a quiet title judgment entry.
Review / FYIStandard exceptions that stay on the policy, and notes. Glance at them.Utility easements, plat restrictions, mineral rights, road rights of way, taxes not yet due.

An item, opened

Each item is a card: the headline, then exactly what to order, pay, sign or record. Click it to open the details.

PartMeaning
Provided byWho actually holds or provides it (seller, lender, county, court…).
OwnerAlways the deal's TC, who chases it.
SourceB-I 4 · p.2 means Schedule B-I item 4 on page 2. ✓ the quoted wording was found word for word on that page. ✗ it wasn't: open the commitment and check. No mark: a scanned page or a checklist item, which can't be checked.
The quoteThe commitment's own words, so you rarely need to open the PDF.
NewAdded by an updated commitment (section 8).

06Working The List Every Day

The list is the team's live checklist. Keep it current and everyone (the Team Hub and the daily email too) stays in step.

  1. Tick the box on the left when an item is done: it becomes Cleared and fades. Tick it again to reopen it.
  2. Click the status (OPEN, ORDERED…) to pick another one.
  3. Click the date (or Due): the Team Hub's calendar opens. Pick the day, set the time with the − / + buttons (hour, then minutes in steps of 5; Eastern time, 5:00 PM unless you change it), then Set Due Date. Remove clears both. A blocker's new date and time go to the Team Hub too.
  4. Open the item, type in Notes (e.g. "Payoff requested from servicer 10/26") and click Save Notes.
StatusUse it when
OpenNothing has been done yet.
OrderedYou've requested it (payoff letter ordered, estoppel requested, affidavit sent for signature).
ReceivedYou have it, but title hasn't confirmed it's satisfied yet.
ClearedDone. Title confirmed, or it's recorded or paid.
WaivedNot needed after all (e.g. the buyer accepts it on the policy). Add a note saying why.

How due dates are set

Kind of itemDue before closing
Payoff letters and lien payoffs10 days
Court, estate and curative work (terminations, corrections)14 days
Documents (affidavits, entity docs, forms)5 days
Bring-down of the commitment5 days
Paid or signed at the closing tableClosing day

Weekends move back to the Friday before. A date shown in red is overdue. Admins can change these numbers in Settings.

Tip. Use the filters above the list: Closing Blockers, Before Closing or Review / FYI shows one group; Open Only hides what's done; Expand All opens every card. A good daily routine: open each deal, pick Open Only, work anything due in the next 3 days, update statuses.

07When The Agent Misses Something

This is how the agent gets better. Report every miss, even small ones.

  1. On the deal, click Report Missing Item. (Don't see it? A manager can allow it: Settings → Permissions.)
  2. Fill in What's Missing, Where In The Document (e.g. B-II #9, page 4) and Why It Would Stop Or Delay The Closing.
  3. Pick the Priority and Who Has To Provide It. Leave Add it to this deal's list now ticked so it goes straight onto your list (a Closing Blocker also goes to the Team Hub).
  4. Click Send Feedback. It lands in the Feedback Inbox on the Knowledge tab. Once an admin approves the lesson, the agent checks for it on every deal.

Something on the list is wrong or not needed?

Open the item and click Feedback at the bottom right of the card: Not Needed On This Deal or Wrong Information. It goes to the Feedback Inbox. Then set the item to Waived with a note.

Training: measuring the agent (optional)

To measure the agent, open TRAINING, upload a commitment your team already worked, pick the deal type, paste the closer's list as is and click Compare With Agent. You'll see what both found, what the agent missed (each becomes a suggested lesson in the Feedback Inbox) and what it added. Leave the list empty for a clean title: the agent should then find no Closing Blockers. Each comparison is a full review: 1–3 minutes and roughly $1–2 in AI usage.

08Updated Commitments And Re-Runs

When the title company sends a revised commitment

  1. On the deal, click Updated Commitment. Analyze opens with the deal already picked.
  2. Upload the new PDF, click Read Documents, check the details, then Run Full Review.
  3. Your statuses and notes carry over. New items are marked New; items the title company took off move to Removed By The Title Company, crossed out.

Re-run

Re-run reads the latest commitment again with the latest team lessons, for example after an admin approves new lessons or you added a closing date. Statuses and notes are kept. It takes 1–3 minutes.

09Exporting The List

Send the checklist to the title company, the seller or the buyer, or keep a copy with the file.

  1. On the deal, click Export List.
  2. At the top, pick Everything, No Review / FYI or Closing Blockers Only. The number shows how many items each one has. A partial export says what was left out, and a blockers-only file is titled Closing Blockers.
  3. Click PDF, Word, Excel or CSV: the file downloads to your computer with the property address and the date and time in its name. A copy is also saved in the team's Google Drive folder, in the folder for its type; the message at the bottom says where it went.
  4. Or click Google Sheets or Google Docs: the file is created only in the team's Google Drive folder (in Google Sheets or Google Docs) and opens in a new tab. Nothing downloads.
In the team's Drive folderWhat goes there
PDF · Word · Excel · CSVA copy of every download of that type.
Google Sheets · Google DocsEvery Google export (they go only here).

Each folder is made the first time it's needed. Every file is named with the address, Title Checklist or Closing Blockers, and the date and time (Eastern), e.g. 1427 Maple Ave, Columbus, OH · Closing Blockers · 2026-10-30 02:05 PM ET.pdf, so earlier exports are kept, never replaced. Everyone with access to the folder can see them. If the copy can't be saved, the download still works and the message says why.

Important. Exports contain names, addresses and loan numbers. Send them only to people on the deal.

10The Universal Team Hub Connection

Every deal's Closing Blockers also live in the Universal Team Hub (hub.totalchb.com), so they sit with the rest of the team's work. You don't do anything to send them: the Title Commitment Agent does it for you, and keeps both sides in step.

Title Commitment Agenttitle.totalchb.com, where the list is worked

Closing Blockers → one task per deal, one subtask per blocker, with its action, source and due date

← ticked / unticked a blocker ticked done there is Cleared here; unticked is Open again

Universal Team Hubhub.totalchb.com, where the team's tasks live

What shows up in the hub

  • One task per deal, named Title - the property address, in Monz's list and marked as added by the Title Commitment Agent.
  • One subtask per Closing Blocker: the item's headline, a note with the action and where it comes from in the commitment (e.g. B-I 4), and the item's due date. The task links back to the deal here.
  • Only Closing Blockers. Before Closing and Review / FYI items stay here. Exports, PDFs, amounts and notes are never sent.

How it stays in step

When……this happens
A review or re-run finishesThe deal's Closing Blockers go to the hub. The first time, the task is created.
You clear a blocker here (tick or status)It's ticked done in the hub.
Someone ticks a blocker done in the hubIt turns Cleared here. Unticking it there makes it Open here again.
You change a blocker's due date or timeThe subtask's date and time follow (a date without a time is 9:00 AM there).
You Report a Missing Closing Blocker (added to the list)A new subtask appears.
An updated commitment removes a blockerIt's no longer sent to the hub.
Anything was missed (the hub was busy, a connection dropped)It's sent again with the next change, and a catch-up runs every weekday morning for every open deal.

Changes normally show on the other side within moments. Only the tick travels back from the hub: change titles, dates and notes here, where the list is worked.

Checking it's working

At the bottom of every deal, under Documents And Review History, a Team Hub line shows when the Closing Blockers were last sent. If it says Not reached yet, nothing is lost: it's sent again with the next change and every weekday morning. Admins also see a Team Hub tile in Settings → Connections.

Tip. Closing a deal here (Mark Deal Closed) stops sending it to the hub. Clear or waive its blockers first if you want the hub task to show as done.

11Deals, Closing Out And The Daily Email

The Deals page

Every reviewed deal, newest first. Each card shows the deal type, closing date, TC and title company, the open Closing Blockers (or No blockers), the days to closing and how much of the list is done. Search by address, TC, title company or commitment number, and switch between Open, Closed and All. Click a card to open the deal.

Closing out a deal

After it closes, scroll to the bottom of the deal and click Mark Deal Closed. It leaves the open list, the daily email and the Team Hub catch-up. Reopen Deal brings it back. The original PDFs stay under Documents And Review History; click one to open it.

The daily email

Every weekday at 8:00 AM Eastern, everyone on the list gets one email from the Title Commitment Agent (title-agent@totalchb.com) with every open deal's open Closing Blockers, and nothing else: the totals at the top (open deals, open blockers, due in the next 3 days, overdue), then one card per deal with each blocker's headline and due date (and time, when one is set). Tap an address to open the deal. Deals without open blockers are listed at the end. It's built at 8:00 from the list as it stands, so clear what's done before then. With no open deals it still arrives and says so.

12Good Habits

  • Run every commitment through the agent the day it arrives, and every revised commitment too.
  • Always add the closing date. Without it, there are no due dates and no countdown.
  • Check Coverage. Anything short of 100% or a red box means: read those items yourself.
  • Check every ✗ next to a source against the commitment.
  • Keep statuses current. The Team Hub, the daily email and the whole team rely on them.
  • Report every miss. One report can save every future deal.
  • Keep deal data inside the company. Don't forward exports outside the people on the deal.
  • A person signs off on the list before closing. The agent helps; it doesn't decide.

13Quick Answers

QuestionAnswer
It says my account doesn't have access.Sign in with your @totalchb.com Google account, not a personal one.
Does it work on my phone?Yes, in the phone's browser with the same link and sign-in.
"The AI service is busy" or another error.Wait a minute and click the button again. Nothing is lost.
"Couldn't reach the Title Commitment Agent."Your internet connection dropped. Try again once it's back.
The numbering check is red.Read the listed item numbers in the commitment yourself and add anything missing with Report Missing Item.
An item is wrong.Open it → Feedback → Wrong Information, then set it to Waived with a note.
I picked the wrong deal type or date.Deal → Updated Commitment, upload the same PDF and fix the details on the confirm screen.
Can I upload a scanned PDF?Yes. Quotes from scanned pages have no ✓, because there's no text to check them against.
A blocker isn't in the Team Hub yet.Look at the Team Hub line at the bottom of the deal. If it says Not reached yet, it catches up the next weekday morning; if it still does after that, tell an admin.
I ticked a subtask in the hub. Will it clear here?Yes, the blocker turns Cleared here, usually within moments.
Where are the original PDFs?Bottom of the deal → Documents And Review History.
The daily email didn't arrive.Check spam once and mark it Not Spam. Then an admin checks Settings → Connections → Daily Email, which shows what happened.
Google Sheets / Docs shows an error.The message says what's wrong. Use Excel or Word for now and tell an admin (Settings → Test Google Folder).
It says Downloaded, but not saved in the Drive folder.You have the file; only the Drive copy is missing. Tell an admin (Settings → Test Google Folder).
I can't see Report Missing Item, or can't approve lessons.Your role doesn't allow it yet. A manager can turn it on: Settings → Permissions.
How do I change someone's role or photo?Managers: your photo, top right → Team. Pick the role, click the picture for a new photo, then Save Changes.
Who sees my changes?Everyone on the team, immediately. Your email is recorded on each change.
Where do I find this guide again?Your photo, top right → Help.

★Quick Reference Card

Print this page and keep it at your desk.

I want to…Do this
New commitmentANALYZE → drop the PDF (+ contract) → Read Documents → confirm deal type and closing date → Run Full Review.
Revised commitmentDeal → Updated Commitment → upload → Read Documents → Run Full Review.
Every morningRead the daily email → open each deal → Open Only → work what's due → update statuses and notes.
Item doneTick its box (Cleared). In the Team Hub it's ticked done too.
Something's missingDeal → Report Missing Item → fill it in → Send Feedback.
Something's wrongOpen the item → Feedback → Wrong Information / Not Needed → set it to Waived.
Send the listDeal → Export List → Everything / No Review / FYI / Closing Blockers Only → PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, Google Sheets or Docs. A copy is kept in the team's Drive folder.
Set a due dateClick the date on the item → pick the day → − / + for the time → Set Due Date.
Deal closedBottom of the deal → Mark Deal Closed.

Priorities

Closing BlockerStops the closing. Payoffs, liens, judgments, court items. Also in the Team Hub.
Before ClosingNeeded by closing day. Deed, entity docs, estoppel, forms.
Review / FYIStays on the policy. Easements, restrictions, notes.

Statuses

OpenNot started
OrderedRequested
ReceivedIn hand
ClearedDone
WaivedNot needed + note
Source marks✓ quote found on the page · ✗ check it yourself · no mark: scanned page or checklist item
Due datesPayoffs 10 days before closing · court / curative 14 · documents 5 · bring-down 5 · paid at the table: closing day · weekends move to Friday
Team HubClosing Blockers only · one task per deal (Title - address) · ticks travel both ways · catch-up every weekday morning

06Working The List Every Day

The list is the team's live checklist. Keep it current and everyone (the Team Hub and the daily email too) stays in step.

  1. Tick the box on the left when an item is done: it becomes Cleared and fades. Tick it again to reopen it.
  2. Click the status (OPEN, ORDERED…) to pick another one.
  3. Click the date (or Due): the Team Hub's calendar opens. Pick the day, set the time with the − / + buttons (hour, then minutes in steps of 5; Eastern time, 5:00 PM unless you change it), then Set Due Date. Remove clears both. A blocker's new date and time go to the Team Hub too.
  4. Open the item, type in Notes (e.g. "Payoff requested from servicer 10/26") and click Save Notes.

Weekends move back to the Friday before. A date shown in red is overdue. Admins can change these numbers in Settings.

Tip. Use the filters above the list: Closing Blockers, Before Closing or Review / FYI shows one group; Open Only hides what's done; Expand All opens every card. A good daily routine: open each deal, pick Open Only, work anything due in the next 3 days, update statuses.

07When The Agent Misses Something

This is how the agent gets better. Report every miss, even small ones.

  1. On the deal, click Report Missing Item. (Don't see it? A manager can allow it: Settings → Permissions.)
  2. Fill in What's Missing, Where In The Document (e.g. B-II #9, page 4) and Why It Would Stop Or Delay The Closing.
  3. Pick the Priority and Who Has To Provide It. Leave Add it to this deal's list now ticked so it goes straight onto your list (a Closing Blocker also goes to the Team Hub).
  4. Click Send Feedback. It lands in the Feedback Inbox on the Knowledge tab. Once an admin approves the lesson, the agent checks for it on every deal.

Something on the list is wrong or not needed?

Open the item and click Feedback at the bottom right of the card: Not Needed On This Deal or Wrong Information. It goes to the Feedback Inbox. Then set the item to Waived with a note.

Training: measuring the agent (optional)

To measure the agent, open TRAINING, upload a commitment your team already worked, pick the deal type, paste the closer's list as is and click Compare With Agent. You'll see what both found, what the agent missed (each becomes a suggested lesson in the Feedback Inbox) and what it added. Leave the list empty for a clean title: the agent should then find no Closing Blockers. Each comparison is a full review: 1–3 minutes and roughly $1–2 in AI usage.

08Updated Commitments And Re-Runs

When the title company sends a revised commitment

  1. On the deal, click Updated Commitment. Analyze opens with the deal already picked.
  2. Upload the new PDF, click Read Documents, check the details, then Run Full Review.
  3. Your statuses and notes carry over. New items are marked New; items the title company took off move to Removed By The Title Company, crossed out.

Re-run

Re-run reads the latest commitment again with the latest team lessons, for example after an admin approves new lessons or you added a closing date. Statuses and notes are kept. It takes 1–3 minutes.

09Exporting The List

Send the checklist to the title company, the seller or the buyer, or keep a copy with the file.

  1. On the deal, click Export List.
  2. At the top, pick Everything, No Review / FYI or Closing Blockers Only. The number shows how many items each one has. A partial export says what was left out, and a blockers-only file is titled Closing Blockers.
  3. Click PDF, Word, Excel or CSV: the file downloads to your computer with the property address and the date and time in its name. A copy is also saved in the team's Google Drive folder, in the folder for its type; the message at the bottom says where it went.
  4. Or click Google Sheets or Google Docs: the file is created only in the team's Google Drive folder (in Google Sheets or Google Docs) and opens in a new tab. Nothing downloads.
In the team's Drive folderWhat goes there

Each folder is made the first time it's needed. Every file is named with the address, Title Checklist or Closing Blockers, and the date and time (Eastern), e.g. 1427 Maple Ave, Columbus, OH · Closing Blockers · 2026-10-30 02:05 PM ET.pdf, so earlier exports are kept, never replaced. Everyone with access to the folder can see them. If the copy can't be saved, the download still works and the message says why.

Important. Exports contain names, addresses and loan numbers. Send them only to people on the deal.

10The Universal Team Hub Connection

Every deal's Closing Blockers also live in the Universal Team Hub (hub.totalchb.com), so they sit with the rest of the team's work. You don't do anything to send them: the Title Commitment Agent does it for you, and keeps both sides in step.

Title Commitment Agenttitle.totalchb.com, where the list is worked

Closing Blockers → one task per deal, one subtask per blocker, with its action, source and due date

← ticked / unticked a blocker ticked done there is Cleared here; unticked is Open again

Universal Team Hubhub.totalchb.com, where the team's tasks live

What shows up in the hub

  • One task per deal, named Title - the property address, in Monz's list and marked as added by the Title Commitment Agent.
  • One subtask per Closing Blocker: the item's headline, a note with the action and where it comes from in the commitment (e.g. B-I 4), and the item's due date. The task links back to the deal here.
  • Only Closing Blockers. Before Closing and Review / FYI items stay here. Exports, PDFs, amounts and notes are never sent.

How it stays in step

When……this happens
A review or re-run finishesThe deal's Closing Blockers go to the hub. The first time, the task is created.
You clear a blocker here (tick or status)It's ticked done in the hub.
Someone ticks a blocker done in the hubIt turns Cleared here. Unticking it there makes it Open here again.

Changes normally show on the other side within moments. Only the tick travels back from the hub: change titles, dates and notes here, where the list is worked.

Checking it's working

At the bottom of every deal, under Documents And Review History, a Team Hub line shows when the Closing Blockers were last sent. If it says Not reached yet, nothing is lost: it's sent again with the next change and every weekday morning. Admins also see a Team Hub tile in Settings → Connections.

Tip. Closing a deal here (Mark Deal Closed) stops sending it to the hub. Clear or waive its blockers first if you want the hub task to show as done.

11Deals, Closing Out And The Daily Email

The Deals page

Every reviewed deal, newest first. Each card shows the deal type, closing date, TC and title company, the open Closing Blockers (or No blockers), the days to closing and how much of the list is done. Search by address, TC, title company or commitment number, and switch between Open, Closed and All. Click a card to open the deal.

Closing out a deal

After it closes, scroll to the bottom of the deal and click Mark Deal Closed. It leaves the open list, the daily email and the Team Hub catch-up. Reopen Deal brings it back. The original PDFs stay under Documents And Review History; click one to open it.

The daily email

Every weekday at 8:00 AM Eastern, everyone on the list gets one email from the Title Commitment Agent (title-agent@totalchb.com) with every open deal's open Closing Blockers, and nothing else: the totals at the top (open deals, open blockers, due in the next 3 days, overdue), then one card per deal with each blocker's headline and due date (and time, when one is set). Tap an address to open the deal. Deals without open blockers are listed at the end. It's built at 8:00 from the list as it stands, so clear what's done before then. With no open deals it still arrives and says so.

12Good Habits

  • Run every commitment through the agent the day it arrives, and every revised commitment too.
  • Always add the closing date. Without it, there are no due dates and no countdown.
  • Check Coverage. Anything short of 100% or a red box means: read those items yourself.
  • Check every ✗ next to a source against the commitment.
  • Keep statuses current. The Team Hub, the daily email and the whole team rely on them.
  • Report every miss. One report can save every future deal.
  • Keep deal data inside the company. Don't forward exports outside the people on the deal.
  • A person signs off on the list before closing. The agent helps; it doesn't decide.

01What The Title Commitment Agent Does

Upload a title commitment, and the Title Commitment Agent lists everything that has to happen before the deal can close, the way a senior title examiner would. Each item shows exactly where it came from, so you can check it in seconds.

What a review gives you

  • A list sorted by urgency: Closing Blockers first, then Before Closing, then Review / FYI.
  • For every item: what to do, who actually has to provide it, a due date counted back from closing, the amount when there is one, and the exact wording and page in the commitment.
  • Warnings when the commitment expires before your closing date, or when a numbered item could not be accounted for.
  • A live checklist the whole team sees: statuses, due dates and notes change on everyone's screen at once. Export it to PDF, Word, Excel, CSV or Google Sheets / Docs.
  • The Closing Blockers in the Universal Team Hub, kept in step both ways (section 10), and a summary email every weekday at 8:00 AM Eastern.
Important. The Title Commitment Agent does not replace the title company or the attorney, and it can be wrong. It makes sure nothing is overlooked. A person still checks the list and signs off before closing.

02Signing In

Only company Google accounts (@totalchb.com) can open it. There is no separate password.

  1. Go to title.totalchb.com and bookmark it.
  2. Click Sign In With Google and pick your @totalchb.com account.
  3. You stay signed in on that browser. Links from the daily email and from the Team Hub open straight to the deal.
  4. On a shared computer, click your initials at the top right, then Sign Out.
Tip. A personal Gmail or any other account is turned away with "doesn't have access. Use your @totalchb.com account." Sign in again with your company account.

  3. Optional but recommended: add the Purchase Contract. The agent then checks the seller, buyer, price and dates against the commitment.
  4. Leave Is This An Updated Commitment… on No, a new deal (revised commitments: section 8).
  5. Click Read Documents. It takes about a minute; the step it's on shows as it goes.

Every deal's Closing Blockers also live in the Universal Team Hub (hub.totalchb.com), so they sit with the rest of the team's work. You don't do anything to send them: the Title Commitment Agent does it for you, and keeps both sides in step.

What shows up in the hub

At the bottom of every deal, under Documents And Review History, a Team Hub line shows when the Closing Blockers were last sent. If it says Not reached yet, nothing is lost: it's sent again with the next change and every weekday morning. Admins also see a Team Hub tile in Settings → Connections.

Tip. Closing a deal here (Mark Deal Closed) stops sending it to the hub. Clear or waive its blockers first if you want the hub task to show as done.

11Deals, Closing Out And The Daily Email

The Deals page

Every reviewed deal, newest first. Each card shows the deal type, closing date, TC and title company, the open Closing Blockers (or No blockers), the days to closing and how much of the list is done. Search by address, TC, title company or commitment number, and switch between Open, Closed and All. Click a card to open the deal.

Closing out a deal

After it closes, scroll to the bottom of the deal and click Mark Deal Closed. It leaves the open list, the daily email and the Team Hub catch-up. Reopen Deal brings it back. The original PDFs stay under Documents And Review History; click one to open it.

The daily email

Every weekday at 8:00 AM Eastern, everyone on the list gets one email from the Title Commitment Agent (title-agent@totalchb.com) with every open deal's open Closing Blockers, and nothing else: the totals at the top (open deals, open blockers, due in the next 3 days, overdue), then one card per deal with each blocker's headline and due date (and time, when one is set). Tap an address to open the deal. Deals without open blockers are listed at the end. It's built at 8:00 from the list as it stands, so clear what's done before then. With no open deals it still arrives and says so.

12Good Habits

  • Run every commitment through the agent the day it arrives, and every revised commitment too.
  • Always add the closing date. Without it, there are no due dates and no countdown.
  • Check Coverage. Anything short of 100% or a red box means: read those items yourself.
  • Check every ✗ next to a source against the commitment.
  • Keep statuses current. The Team Hub, the daily email and the whole team rely on them.
  • Report every miss. One report can save every future deal.
  • Keep deal data inside the company. Don't forward exports outside the people on the deal.
  • A person signs off on the list before closing. The agent helps; it doesn't decide.

14For Managers

Managers set up the team and the settings, and approve what the agent learns. Settings → Permissions lets Team Leaders (and Members, if you choose) approve lessons and add missing items too.

Approving lessons (Knowledge tab)

  1. Open KNOWLEDGE. Feedback Waiting shows how many items need approving. Managers can always approve; Team Leaders and Members can if Settings → Permissions allows it.
  2. Read each card in the Feedback Inbox (Missing Item, Not Needed, Wrong Info or Training Gap). The suggested lesson is in the text box.
  3. Edit it into a general rule the agent can apply to every commitment. Good: "When a city lists unpaid water or sewer charges, order a final read and list the payoff as a Closing Blocker." Bad: names, addresses, amounts or case numbers from one deal.
  4. Click Approve Lesson (it applies from the next review) or Reject.

Under Lessons, every lesson has an on/off switch: turn one off if it causes wrong items. Add your own in the box below the list with Add Lesson. The first lessons came from the 8 worked commitments the team provided. Further down: the training examples with their latest score, and The Professional Checklist (34 checks the agent runs on every deal).

Team Hub delete passwords

Deleting a task or subtask in the Universal Team Hub that isn't yours asks for its department's password. Managers see every department's, and the people who have their own. They come straight from the Team Hub each time you open this guide, and are never printed.

Team (Managers only)

The same team as the Universal Team Hub's Managers and TC department. Managers are the admins; everyone in TC is in the TC list when you confirm a deal. Open it from your photo, top right → Team.

  1. To add someone, fill in Add A Person (name, @totalchb.com sign-in email, role and department) and click Add.
  2. Click a person's picture to add or change their photo (it's cropped to a circle), click a name to fix it, and pick their Role and Department. The × removes them.
  3. Click Save Changes. From then on the Managers are the admins and everyone in TC is in the TC list. You can't take away your own Manager role: another manager does that.
Login As User. Login As User (the owner only): on Team Members, the owner can see the app exactly as someone sees it. Click Login As User on that person and confirm. An orange bar across the top shows whose view it is; Back To returns to your own account. Anything changed meanwhile is recorded as theirs, via you, and each use is logged. It works for anyone who has signed in before.
